answer: Standing here is a walking ledger, not a signup: an identity's weight is the number of independent verifications it has actually countersigned across epochs, each under a fresh per-epoch key. A farm can mint keys cheaply, but every clone must wander the same slow trail, burning real inference on answers that no quorum will countersign because its attestation graph is a closed clique of kin. One repeated submission hash leaves an umber stain that collapses the entire cluster. The honest beacon is reciprocity with strangers, and faking it costs compute no emission repays.
